plant.culled_by: TWO INDEPENDENT EYES. Rafe, device walk, 2026-09-06; and round 30's blind seat, 2026-09-06.
plant.verbatim: flat pale block, no interior texture (seat) / too shiny on worn areas, character washed out (Rafe)

seat.BEST_WHY: The wall band across y≈388–422 is the only place in the deck where structure was authored rather than filled. The vertical timber at x≈266 runs y=386→421 and *breaks the wall's top silhouette* — it stands proud into the black at y=380, so it reads as a post driven through the course and left long. Three horizontal ties cross it at y≈396, 404, 412 and they are three different lengths (the middle one runs ~10px, the outer two ~6px), which is what a lashed repair looks like and what a stamped cross does not. A second timber at x≈355 is shorter and carries no ties; a third at x≈416 is a horizontal bar with a stepped right end. Spacing between the three is 89px then 61px — irregular, i.e. placed where something failed, not on a grid. The wall's top edge is also stepped rather than run: it lifts ~30px at x≈470 and the corridor mouth at x≈500–545 has jambs at different depths (left at y≈422, right at y≈390). That asymmetry is the single most convincing thing in any of the four frames — it is the only evidence anywhere that the place was built and then patched by someone who didn't care how it looked.
seat.WORST_WHY:
Three separate glance-level failures, any one of which is disqualifying.

1. The green pool is a flat rectangle laid on top of the dirt. Sampling row y=60: x=247 is dirt `(85,47,20)`, x=248 is water `(36,76,62)` — one pixel, no transition, no bank, no edging tile. Its bottom edge at column x=300 does the same thing between y=191 and y=192. Every one of the ~5,500 water pixels is the identical value `(36,76,62)`; there is no depth gradient, no shallow margin, nothing under the surface. It is a filled marquee selection.

2. The stated lighting model is entirely absent. Mean luminance of the top-left 20×20 corner is 85.4, top-right 88.2, bottom-left 78.5 — and the 20×20 block around the figure at the top is **55.6**. The frame is *brighter at its edges than at the light-carrier*. There is no falloff, no pool, no direction.

3. Nothing has weight. The two barrels at (128,200) and (172,200) sit across the dirt/cobble seam with zero contact shadow; the crates at (68,10) and (68,58) are pixel-identical copies of one sprite with the same dark plank tile repeated verbatim beneath each; the green moss blob at (25,60) reappears unrotated at (30,207) and at (367,157). And the orc sprite carries a hard black outline at a larger effective pixel size than any environment element, which has none — it is visibly a different asset from a different set.

flip_list: The figure carrying "the only light there is" is not the brightest thing in the frame. Its brightest pixel measures 193.7; the floor at (442,485) immediately to its right measures 193.3. Regrade the sprite so its lit side sits at least 40 luminance above the floor it stands on.

The shield at (415–432, 478–500) has been graded to a mud-brown at the same value as the surrounding flagstone, so the figure's silhouette breaks apart at a glance. Give the shield face its own value separation — rim dark, face light — independent of the light pass.

The wall course's bottom edge at y≈452 is a single unbroken dead-straight dark line running from x=183 to x=500 without one break, step or interruption, and its top edge at y≈423 is dead-parallel to it. Break the run: step it, drop a course, let a stone sit proud.

The band above that line, x=190→500 by y=390→420, is ~9,000px of undifferentiated soft brown with no joint, block or edge in it — the largest empty area in the frame. Either put the course structure up there or drop it out of the light.

The vertical timbers at x≈266 and x≈355 sit fully inside the band and touch no silhouette, so they read as painted marks on a surface rather than posts driven through it. Extend them past the wall's top edge as in the other frames.

Two incompatible floor systems meet at x≈470–480 (y 460–640) with no seam: left of it is a regular ~35px square grid with pale 1px joints, right of it is irregular flagstone of mixed sizes with dark joints. Add an actual boundary — a threshold course, a step, a change in level — or unify the two.

The 3-stroke diagonal scratch glyph in the right-hand flagstone repeats unrotated at roughly (565,500), (530,565), (605,510), (555,610), (700,610) and (505,655) — same angle, same stroke count, same length every time. Vary the angle and count, or cut the count to a third and place them where traffic would actually be.

The floor patch at x 230–320, y 545–650 carries a distinct greenish-grey cast against the warm tan of its neighbours, with no object, stain edge or joint explaining it. Either give it a cause (a stain with a boundary) or remove the tint.

The black regions are literally `(2,2,2)` flat with axis-aligned razor edges — the vertical cut at x=630 from y=135 to y=380 goes from lit wall to absolute black in one column. Give the wall's near edge a 1–2px rim value so the void reads as an unlit room rather than a hole in the canvas.

Nothing in the frame casts a shadow: not the wall onto the floor, not the object at (300–380, 640–710), not the figure. Add at minimum a contact shadow under the figure and a cast band under the wall's near face.
law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
